items.followUp: Differentiate between accuracy and precision in scientific observations.

rubric.why: Qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics without numerical measurements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that qualitative observations are descriptive or non-numerical.

rubric.why: Quantitative observations involve measurements expressed numerically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that quantitative observations involve measurements or numerical values.

modelAnswer: Qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics and are not expressed numerically.
Quantitative observations involve measurements and are expressed in numbers.

items.followUp: What happens to the amount of DNA and the number of chromosomes during S phase?

rubric.why: DNA is replicated during the synthesis (S) phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA is copied, duplicated, or replicated.

rubric.why: DNA content doubles as each chromosome forms two sister chromatids, while chromosome number remains unchanged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA content doubles or sister chromatids form, and that chromosome number remains unchanged.

modelAnswer: During the S phase, DNA is replicated.
The DNA content doubles and each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids, but the chromosome number remains unchanged.

items.followUp: How do germ-line cells give rise to gametes?

rubric.why: Somatic cells are body cells that form the tissues and organs of an organism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying somatic cells as body cells.

rubric.why: Germ-line cells give rise to gametes, generally through meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that germ-line cells produce or give rise to gametes.

modelAnswer: Somatic cells are the body cells that form the tissues and organs of an organism.
Germ-line cells give rise to gametes, usually by meiosis.
